items.title: Trump says Iran sent 'big present' as US prepares troop surge
items.description: Donald Trump repeats claims that the United States is negotiating with Iran to end the war, as the Pentagon reportedly prepares to deploy thousands more troops to the Middle East.

items.title: Israel's Lebanon plan could strengthen Hezbollah. Here's what you should know
items.description: The focus of the Middle East war shifts to Lebanon as Israel plans to occupy southern parts of the country.

items.title: Israel says it is planning to occupy southern Lebanon
items.description: Israel's defence minister has announced plans for his country's military to take control of southern Lebanon, from the Israeli border, known as the Blue Line, to the Litani River.

items.title: Live: Air strikes batter Iran as it attacks Israel and Gulf states, diplomatic efforts gather pace
items.description: US President Donald Trump says the United States is talking to "the right people" in Iran in an effort to end hostilities and claims the Iranians want to reach a deal very badly. Follow live.

items.title: 'Something really shifted': Inside the software company that laid off 40pc of its staff
items.description: As big tech companies sack staff and say AI will pick up the slack, workers are left to grapple with what's really going on.

items.title: Waste collectors warn bin services may stop if diesel not found soon
items.description: Waste collectors say they are struggling to acquire diesel and many are operating at "unsustainable" losses, putting the collection of household bins and commercial waste under threat.

items.title: In Australia's most food insecure suburbs, lines for aid are doubling
items.description: Most areas across Australia are dealing with food insecurity as food relief services say demand is growing. It comes as experts warn the price of groceries are likely to increase due to the war in the Middle East.

items.title: They lived in spare rooms and motels, their teen years 'stripped away'
items.description: Spare bedrooms, couches, and cars hide the stories of Australia's youth homeless crisis. But they are stories that also reveal a grit and ambition to defy the statistics.

items.title: Tropical Cyclone Narelle re-forms off WA, expected to reach category three
items.description: Having cut a swathe across northern Australia over the past week, Tropical Cyclone Narelle is now threatening coastal communities in Western Australia.

items.title: E-bike power crackdown and age limits introduced in NSW
items.description: The NSW government has recently announced staged reforms to improve safety for e-bike riders and pedestrians. This is what it'll mean for the community.

items.title: 'So lucky': Burke warns failed Perth bomb attack could have killed many
items.description: The home affairs minister says Australia was "so lucky" to avoid mass casualties during the attempted Australia Day bomb attack in Perth and admits the nation was slow to recognise the gravity of the alleged terrorist act.

items.title: Married at First Sight expert Mel Schilling dies, aged 54
items.description: Schilling's husband, Gareth Brisbane, took to social media on Tuesday night to reveal the news.

items.title: Live: Labor says it is 'way too soon' to talk about fuel rationing
items.description: The government says it is "too soon" to be talking about fuel rationing as the war in the Middle East disrupts supply. Follow live.

items.title: NDIS participants work more and feel better after accessing the scheme
items.description: New analysis by the e61 Institute, which tracks NDIS participants over more than a decade, finds substantial improvements to their workforce participation and self-reported energy levels within four years of accessing the taxpayer-funded scheme.

items.title: A severed body part found in a dead crocodile kickstarts the new Deadloch
items.description: Kate McLennan and Kate McCartney (Get Krack!n) set out to make a "funny Broadchurch" with crime comedy Deadloch. Now, with fans around the world, it's back for season two.

items.title: Vivid dreams can make you feel like you've had a deep sleep: study
items.description: People woken during vivid and immersive dreaming feel like they've had a deep sleep — even when their brain is in a lighter sleep state, according to a new study.

items.title: Travel quiz: Do you have the stamina to complete this trip?
items.description: Which country has the dong as its currency? And where would you dine on tteokbokki?

items.title: Location of Brisbane's new Olympic stadium unveiled
items.description: New artist impressions showing the interior of the 63,000-seat arena have also been released.

items.title: Alleged bank robber arrested after 30 years on the run
items.description: A man wanted by police over two bank robberies in NSW almost 30 years ago has been arrested and charged.

items.title: 'I demand discipline': Why Labor's second term could be harder than its first
items.description: Despite holding an overwhelming majority in parliament, the Malinauskas government faces no shortage of policy and political challenges to navigate in its second term.

items.title: UTAS got what it wanted on land sales, but its problems may run deeper
items.description: The University of Tasmania's reaction to a proposed restriction on its land sales was swift and effective, emails obtained under Right to Information show. It now has one last step to overcome, with a vote in parliament expected this week.

items.title: Russia fires nearly 400 drones at Ukraine, with UNESCO site damaged
items.description: Three were killed and 30 wounded in a rare daytime attack, including on the city of Lviv, while four have been killed in an overnight bombardment.

items.title: Former nurse Sarah Mullally tasked with healing a wounded Anglican Church
items.description: When Sarah Mullally is installed as the leader of the Church of England this week, many senior clerics won't be in attendance. For some, it's because she's a woman.

items.title: Wine growers fear smoke taint will spoil harvest as planned burns begin
items.description: Just months after devastating bushfires, wine growers are concerned planned burns in regional Victoria pose a new risk to their grapes.

items.title: Queensland mulch company says 'political agenda' behind council rejection
items.description: Queensland's waste industry has blasted a local council's "political agenda" over a decision requiring an odorous wood mulching site at Ipswich to be covered up quickly.
